tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. It was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it was not used.) After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Version I chose:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc is newer, but it was only ever healthy in staging, so it didn't count.
- **Rollback:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0. I checked afterwards: the service shows healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and has paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result after the rollback. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent production-healthy release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it doesn't qualify).
